summary.text: Ashleigh Vandenberg is an independent candidate for Sydenham at the 2026 Victorian election. A registered nurse whose specialties include vascular, thoracic and intensive care nursing, she has sat on Melton City Council since 2020. Beyond that, the ABC's note had little biographical detail as at early November 2026.

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC says she has been a councillor since 2020 but doesn't give the label she stood under; recorded with her current party code.

sources.title: Sydenham: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Joh Bauch is One Nation's candidate for Sydenham at the 2026 Victorian election. A Brimbank councillor since the 2024 council elections, he holds business and law qualifications and has worked in migration law and run a media business. This is his fifth tilt at state or federal parliament: he stood for the Liberals in Niddrie and in the federal seat of Jagajaga in 2010, and as an independent in Tarneit in 2014 and Kororoit in 2022.

previous_candidacies.note: The sources say he stood but don't state the result; recorded as lost because he wasn't elected.
The ABC says he stood but doesn't give the result; recorded as lost because he wasn't elected.
The ABC says he was elected in 2024 but doesn't give the label he stood under; recorded with his current party code.

summary.text: Maggie Jane is the Greens candidate for Sydenham at the 2026 Victorian election. She is a social worker and a carer. She says the idea of standing came to her during a traffic jam on Taylors Road, and she is campaigning on living costs, transport and roads, and government accountability.

priorities.text: Sydenham has been neglected for too long
Easing the cost of living and making housing more affordable
Upgrading local roads and improving transport
Holding government to account for ordinary people

summary.text: Maria Kerr is running as an independent in Sydenham at the 2026 Victorian election. A Brimbank City councillor since 2020, she has previously stood for the Liberals, in Sydenham in 2018 and in St Albans in 2022. Her family migrated from Italy during the 1950s, and she studied business management before working in insurance.

occupation.note: The ABC says she has worked in the insurance industry without giving a job title.

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC says she was elected to Brimbank council in 2020 but doesn't give the label she stood under; recorded with her current party code.

summary.text: Matthew De Angelis is an independent candidate for Sydenham at the 2026 Victorian election. He calls himself an investigative researcher and founder, with about 15 years in business, media and marketing, and runs the media studio Common Monster. The ABC notes he co-founded a startup and has worked as a stand-up comedian; his campaign site publishes research and reform proposals on local issues.

prior_roles.note: His site describes Common Monster as his IP and entertainment media studio.

summary.text: Nancy G Croes, listed by her party as Nancy Croes, is the Family First candidate for Sydenham at the 2026 Victorian election. Born and raised in Aruba, she has lived in Victoria for about 11 years and holds a communication degree from East Carolina University in the United States. She worked in communication and marketing in Aruba and is now a self-employed pet carer and sales and marketing consultant.

occupation.text: Self-employed pet carer and sales and marketing consultant

summary.text: Nathalie Moussi is the Liberal candidate for Sydenham at the 2026 Victorian election. She has run a small family business in Sydenham for about 15 years. According to the ABC she has also been managing director of a restaurant and a sales manager for genetic technology companies.

priorities.text: Lower crime and lower living costs for local families
A government that delivers, as part of the Liberals' pitch for a fresh start

summary.text: Shania Khan is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Sydenham at the 2026 Victorian election. She drives trains on Melbourne's metropolitan network, belongs to the Rail, Tram and Bus Union and has always lived in the city's western suburbs. She describes herself as an anti-racism campaigner.

priorities.text: I want to take up a real fight against the cost of living crisis
Better public transport, including station parking and bus timetables
More money for local schools and hospitals
Opposing a proposed large AI data centre at Plumpton

summary.text: Uros Rasic is Labor's candidate for Sydenham at the 2026 Victorian election, where the sitting Labor MP, Natalie Hutchins, is retiring. He has been employed at the Parliament of Victoria since 2013 and studied at La Trobe University. Labor describes him as a local whose parents migrated to Australia and settled in Melbourne's west.

prior_roles.note: The ABC says he has worked at the Parliament since 2013 without naming the role.

priorities.text: Spending on local roads and building more schools
Tackling youth crime, including early intervention programs
Free public transport for under-18s every day and for seniors at weekends
